q: An auditor concludes that inventory is materially misstated by Rs 8 crore against profit before tax of Rs 60 crore, and the misstatement is confined to that one balance. The appropriate opinion is:
o: Qualified opinion, as the effect is material but not pervasive
Adverse opinion, as Rs 8 crore is significant against the profit
Disclaimer of opinion, as management refuses to adjust the figure
Unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph added
why: Under SA 705 a qualified opinion is given when misstatements are material but not pervasive to the financial statements. A confined misstatement in one balance is not pervasive, and an Emphasis of Matter can never substitute for a required modification.

q: An auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about a subsidiary that represents 70 percent of consolidated net assets and 80 percent of consolidated revenue. The appropriate report is:
o: Qualified opinion, as the limitation relates to a single component
Adverse opinion, as the amounts involved are large in the accounts
Disclaimer of opinion, as the possible effects are material and pervasive
Unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph on the component
why: Under SA 705 an inability to obtain evidence whose possible effects are material and pervasive results in a disclaimer of opinion. An adverse opinion applies to detected misstatements, not to a scope limitation, and the size of the component here makes the effect pervasive.

q: Under SA 705, pervasive effects are those that, in the auditor judgement:
o: Exceed the overall materiality level by three times or more
Are not confined to specific elements, or are a substantial proportion
Relate to any item reported as a Key Audit Matter in the report
Arise from failure to maintain adequate books of account
why: SA 705 defines pervasive through three situations, effects that are not confined to specific elements, effects that if confined represent or could represent a substantial proportion of the financial statements, and in relation to disclosures those that are fundamental to users understanding. There is no arithmetic multiple of materiality.

q: Under SA 701, communication of Key Audit Matters in the auditor report is mandatory for:
o: All companies whose accounts are audited under the Companies Act 2013
Listed entity audits of complete general purpose financial statements
Companies whose paid-up share capital exceeds Rs 10 crore at year end
Audits where the auditor has issued a modified opinion on the statements
why: SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities and where the auditor otherwise decides or is required by law or regulation to communicate Key Audit Matters. It is not driven by capital size, and KAM reporting is independent of whether the opinion is modified.

q: An auditor issues a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements of a listed company. In relation to Key Audit Matters, the auditor should:
o: Report all Key Audit Matters in the usual separate KAM section
Omit the Key Audit Matters section unless law or regulation requires it
Report only those Key Audit Matters that gave rise to the disclaimer of opinion
Convert every Key Audit Matter into an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
why: SA 705 states that when the auditor disclaims an opinion, the report must not include a Key Audit Matters section unless the auditor is required by law or regulation to do so, because doing so would suggest the statements are more credible than the disclaimer implies.

q: A matter that gives rise to a qualified opinion is, by definition:
o: Always also described in full in the Key Audit Matters section
A key audit matter, but described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion
Never a key audit matter, since it is a modification of the opinion given
Reported as an Emphasis of Matter paragraph instead of elsewhere
why: SA 701 explains that a matter giving rise to a modified opinion is by its nature a key audit matter, but it is not described in the Key Audit Matters section. The report describes it in the Basis for Modification section and the KAM section refers to it.

q: The distinguishing feature of an Emphasis of Matter paragraph under SA 706 is that it refers to a matter:
o: Appropriately disclosed and fundamental to users understanding
Not disclosed in the statements but relevant to understanding the audit
That the auditor was unable to audit for want of sufficient evidence
That will feature in the Key Audit Matters section of the next year
why: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws attention to a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements that in the auditor judgement is of such importance that it is fundamental to users understanding. A matter not disclosed in the financial statements but relevant to the audit is dealt with in an Other Matter paragraph.

q: The financial statements of a company for the current year were audited by the present auditor, and the prior year figures were audited by a predecessor auditor whose report is not being reissued. Under SA 710 read with SA 706, the auditor should:
o: Add an Emphasis of Matter paragraph describing the predecessor audit
Modify the current year opinion as prior figures were audited by another
Add an Other Matter paragraph with the opinion type and its date
Make no reference, corresponding figures not being the auditor concern
why: Where corresponding figures were audited by a predecessor auditor and that report is not reissued, SA 710 requires an Other Matter paragraph stating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor, the type of opinion expressed and the date of that report. Emphasis of Matter relates to matters within the financial statements themselves.

q: Where a material uncertainty related to going concern exists and is adequately disclosed in the financial statements, SA 570 requires the auditor to:
o: Issue a qualified opinion with a separate going concern paragraph
Include the matter as an Emphasis of Matter paragraph in the report
Give an unmodified opinion with a separate Material Uncertainty section
Disclaim the opinion because the future outcome remains uncertain
why: When the use of the going concern basis is appropriate and a material uncertainty exists that is adequately disclosed, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a separate section under the heading Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern. Since the revision of SA 570 this is a dedicated section, not an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.

q: Management prepares the financial statements on a going concern basis, but the auditor concludes that the entity will be liquidated and the going concern basis is inappropriate. The auditor should:
o: Express an adverse opinion on the financial statements as a whole
Express a qualified opinion with a Material Uncertainty section
Disclaim the opinion on the financial statements as a whole
Express an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter added
why: If the financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis but in the auditor judgement that basis is inappropriate, SA 570 requires an adverse opinion, because the basis of preparation itself pervades the entire financial statements.

q: A material uncertainty related to going concern exists but management refuses to make adequate disclosure of it in the financial statements. The auditor should:
o: Disclose the matter in the auditor report and give an unmodified opinion
Withdraw from the engagement in all such cases without reporting
Give a qualified or adverse opinion and state the uncertainty exists
Add a Material Uncertainty section and give an unmodified opinion
why: Where disclosure of a material uncertainty is inadequate, SA 570 requires a qualified or adverse opinion depending on materiality and pervasiveness, and the Basis for Qualified or Adverse Opinion section must state that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the entity ability to continue as a going concern.

q: Under Section 143(3) of the Companies Act 2013, the auditor report must state, among other matters, whether:
o: The company has complied with all the tax laws applicable to it
The company has maintained an adequate cash flow forecast for the year
The internal audit function of the company is adequate for its size
Any director is disqualified under Section 164(2) of the Act
why: Section 143(3) requires reporting on whether any director is disqualified from being appointed as a director under Section 164(2), along with matters such as adequacy of books of account, agreement of financial statements with the books, compliance with accounting standards and adequacy of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements. Tax compliance generally is not a Section 143(3) matter.

q: Under Section 143(12) read with the rules, an auditor who has reason to believe an offence of fraud involving an amount of Rs 2 crore or more is being or has been committed against the company by officers or employees must:
o: Report to the Board or audit committee for their reply, then to the Central Government
Report directly to the Central Government within two days without informing the Board
Report to the audit committee alone, the Central Government being informed by the Board
Report the fraud in the CARO annexure to the report and take no other action on it
why: The auditor must first report the matter to the Board or audit committee within two days of knowledge seeking their reply or observations within forty five days, and then forward the report, reply and comments to the Central Government within fifteen days of receipt of the reply. Frauds below Rs 1 crore are reported to the audit committee or Board instead.

q: An identified or suspected fraud involving an amount below the Section 143(12) reporting threshold must be:
o: Reported to the Central Government in Form ADT-4 in every such case
Ignored altogether where it is not material to the financial statements
Reported only in the CARO annexure to the auditor report on accounts
Reported to the audit committee or Board and disclosed in the Board report
why: Where the fraud involves an amount less than the prescribed threshold, the auditor reports the matter to the audit committee or the Board, specifying the nature of the fraud, the approximate amount and the parties involved, and the details are disclosed in the Board report. Form ADT-4 is used only for Central Government reporting above the threshold.

q: Under SA 700, the Auditor Responsibilities for the Audit of the Financial Statements section must state that the auditor:
o: Guarantees that the financial statements are free from any fraud
Provides limited assurance in accordance with Standards on Auditing
Obtains absolute assurance for error and reasonable assurance for fraud
Obtains reasonable assurance about freedom from material misstatement
why: SA 700 requires the report to state that the objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and that reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance but is not a guarantee. Absolute assurance is never provided.

q: Under SA 700 the ordering of report sections is prescribed. The correct sequence at the start of the auditor report is:
o: Basis for Opinion, then Opinion, followed by Key Audit Matters
Opinion, then Key Audit Matters, followed by Basis for Opinion
Key Audit Matters, then Opinion, then Basis for Opinion
Opinion, then Basis for Opinion, then Key Audit Matters
why: SA 700 requires the Opinion section to be placed first, followed immediately by the Basis for Opinion section, and where applicable the Key Audit Matters section follows. Placing the basis before the opinion reverses the required order.

q: The Basis for Opinion section under SA 700 must include a statement that the auditor:
o: Is independent of the entity under the applicable Code of Ethics
Has verified one hundred percent of the transactions of the entity
Accepts no responsibility to any third party relying on the report
Has relied entirely on management written representations
why: SA 700 requires the Basis for Opinion section to state that the audit was conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing, refer to the auditor responsibilities section, include a statement of independence in accordance with the relevant ethical requirements, and state whether the evidence obtained is sufficient and appropriate.

q: The auditor issued a qualified opinion in the prior year on a matter that remains unresolved and continues to affect the current year figures. Under SA 710, in the current year report the auditor should:
o: Express an unmodified opinion, the qualification being of the prior year
Repeat the prior year auditor report as an annexure to the current one
Add an Other Matter paragraph referring to the prior year qualification
Modify the opinion, referring to current and corresponding figures
why: Under SA 710 for corresponding figures, if the matter giving rise to the prior period modification is unresolved, the auditor modifies the current period opinion and the Basis for Modification refers to both the current period figures and the corresponding figures where the matter affects their comparability.
